To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we designed and developed a generic scene generator that can generate complex 3D synthetic scenes that include the effects of surface heterogeneity, topographic effects and atmospheric effects.

we designed and implemented a generic 3-D scene generator that is capable of generating consistent high spatial, spectral, and temporal resolution top-of-atomsphere radiance scenes that combine surface, topography, and atmospheric effects, and that it was implemented in the FLEX E2ES tool to support the FLEX/Sentinal-3 tandem mission.
we developed and implemented a new generic scene generator for passive optical missions, which was successfully applied to the ESA’s FELX/Sentinel-2 Tandem mission.

the design and implementation of a generic 3-D scene generator for passive optical missions, which is able to produce consistent high resolution synthetic scenes for different instruments and can be adapted to any future mission.
the design and implementation of the GSG for the generation of synthetic scenes of high fidelity for the ESA’s Sentinel-3 FLEX mission.
the development of a generic scene generation tool that is flexible and modular and allows generating synthetic scenes for a large number of instruments and missions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed GSG design and implementation is an appropriate tool to generate synthetic scenes for passive optical missions.

this GSG can be used to generate consistent scenes for multiple instruments of different types (active and passive), with high spatial and spectral resolutions and for different viewing and illumination geometries.

the proposed design and implementation of the GSG is a valuable tool for assessing the mission requirements fulfillment and for validating the data processing chain performance before the mission is launched.

a generic scene generator has been developed and implemented within the E2ES tool for the FLEX/Sentinet-3 tandem mission, allowing to simulate and analyze the expected performance of the FLEX instrument and the data products derived from it, as well as its compatibility with the other instruments of the mission.
the developed generic scene generator is capable of generating consistent high spatial resolution synthetic scenes for multiple instruments of the same mission and for different missions.
the GSG is a flexible and generic tool that can be used for a wide variety of missions and instruments.

the proposed GSG design and its implementation in the FLEX E2ES software are a generic and flexible solution for generating synthetic scenes that can be easily adapted to different missions and instruments.
the proposed design can be applied to any passive mission, including future ones.
